messages:
alex: noticed a p99 jump in staging after the model onboard this morning (v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0). Canary traffic shows 40% higher tail latency. anyone else seeing this?
maria: yup saw it too. baseline p99 was ~220ms, now ~310-350ms depending on batch. p50 looks OK.
bench-bot: CI perf check failed on 1748297000 for pr #4821. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/4821
jon: rough eyeball: kernel selection logs look different for the new checkpoint. seems to prefer the slower attention kernel for longer sequences.
alex: can you paste the kernel selection snippet?
maria: grabbing logs...

maria: ```
[INFO] kernel_selector: seq_len=256 chosen_kernel=attn_generic_sm_v2 cost=12.1
[INFO] kernel_selector: seq_len=64 chosen_kernel=attn_opt_v1 cost=9.2
[INFO] kernel_selector: seq_len=128 chosen_kernel=attn_generic_sm_v2 cost=10.8
```

maria: previously for same shape we were hitting attn_opt_v1 more often.
sam: I also see KV cache hit-rate drop from 0.92 -> 0.71 on canary. seems like tokenization produced slightly longer prefixes (extra BOS tokens), so cache keys don't match.
jon: aha tokenizer change in that PR added a prefix sentinel byte for safety. PR 4821 touched tokenizer + model config. Could be causing different sequence segmentation.
perf-ci: perf regression details: p95 +18%, p99 +35%, average latency +8%. workload: chat-short + batch_size sweep attached. https://perfdash/internal/174829/summary
ops: can we pause the canary rollout?
deploy-bot: @ops requested: rollback canary to v2.4.1. Rollback queued.
alex: before full rollback can we bisect which commit in the PR is the culprit? maybe revert tokenizer change only.
jon: quick bisect plan: revert tokenizer sentinel -> run small repro w/ replay for 10k requests, check kernel_selector histogram. commits: a1b2c3d (tokenizer), b2c3d4e (config bump), c3d4e5f (quant config). suspect a1b2c3d.
maria: I ran a local replay removing the sentinel; kernel selection profile reverted back, and kv cache hit-rate returned to ~0.9. smaller perf run, but consistent.
bench-bot: local microbenchmark: before (v2.4.1) p99=220ms, after full PR p99=350ms, after revert tokenizer p99=225ms.
jon: sounds like tokenizer change breaks cache key normalization (extra byte alters token ids). fallback kernel selection then favors generic kernel for longer sequences due to different tokenization length distribution.
sam: quick mitigation: adjust batcher to cap max_input_length for batching heuristic to avoid mixing long prefixes with short ones; that should reduce worst-case tail while we revert.
alex: agree. action items: 1) ops: pause canary (deploy-bot did). 2) eng-runtime (jon/maria/sam): open revert-only PR for tokenizer change and run CI perf. 3) eng/bench: run 100k replay smoke on canary traffic after revert. 4) product/qa: hold release until perf confirmed.
jon: created issue ENG-2987 and PR draft: r/4821-revert-tokenizer-a1b2. CI perf job queued.
maria: added reproducer and logs to issue, included kernel_selector dump and kv cache stats.
ops: rollback completed to v2.4.1 on canary and stopped further rollout.
perf-ci: post-rollback perf job results: p99 back to 222ms, kv hit 0.91. linking results: https://perfdash/internal/174829/post-rollback
alex: thanks all. keep the revert PR moving and let's add a regression test that compares KV cache key normalization across tokenizer variants. also add a unit check for kernel_selector heuristics so we catch selection shifts when tokenization distributions change.
sam: noted. I'll add batcher cap as a temporary knob on canary config to reduce tail until revert is fully validated.
jon: will re-run canary smoke after PR merge and mark for gradual rollout with observability gating.
alex: closing here — follow ENG-2987 for updates. :white_check_mark:
